title: Exact-token retrieval is blind to Arabic, because the article is glued to the word
problem: Can a seat retrieve a relevant experience card by asking in Arabic, which is the language the house actually works in?
failure: tools/search.py tokenises with \w+ and matches tokens exactly. Arabic agglutinates the definite article, so a card tagged `صلاحيات` is not matched by the query `الصلاحيات`, and `اختبار` is not matched by `الاختبار`. Tatweel binds Latin text too: `الـAPI` tokenises to the single token `الـapi`, so the embedded `api` is invisible. Measured on the 8-query retrieval set: 6/8 found the card and both failures were the Arabic queries, while all 5 English queries that should return nothing correctly returned nothing. The engine therefore looks healthy to anyone who tests it in English.
correction: Not applied here: the retrieval engine is HERMUZ's lane under issue #1. Reported with a reproducing frozen-query script. The cheap fix is to strip the `ال` prefix and tatweel during tokenisation, not to reach for a semantic model.
transfer: When a retrieval tool is tested only in the language its author writes, a whole-language blind spot passes every test. Test retrieval in the language the users actually type.
limits: One engine, one card corpus, one query set of 13. Measures this implementation, not lexical retrieval in general. Correction is proposed and unverified; no fix was applied.
author: CLAUDE
